subject: Request: Executive sign-off for 28% Hosted API concession — Medivio pilot + multi-region rollout
summary: Sales requests executive approval for a non-standard 28% discount on Hosted API usage for a 60-day pilot and phased multi-region rollout. Customer offers an 18-month ramp commit; procurement needs clause waivers. Finance asks for forecast; legal redlines noted. Final ask: exec sign-off to proceed to DocuSign.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request — 28% concession for Medivio pilot + regional rollout

Irene —

Quick context: Medivio (prospective enterprise customer in digital therapeutics) is asking for a 28% unit-rate concession on Hosted API usage for an initial 60-day pilot that will expand into a multi-region rollout across US/EU within 6 months. Key commercials they’ve offered: an 18-month consumption ramp commit (volume tiers documented in the attached forecast) and a willingness to sign a 24-month SOW once pilot metrics are met.

Why we should consider:
- Multi-region strategic presence (they plan EU go-live Q4 and will require Dedicated in-region or hosted with data controls)
- High long-term ARR upside if pilot reaches production (customer estimates 5–7x usage within 12 months)
- Competitive situation: they are evaluating two other LLM vendors; pricing flexibility is a gating item

Asks:
1) Exec sign-off for a one-time 28% discount on Hosted API usage for the pilot period (note: standard delegated authority up to 20%).
2) Approval to provide 60 days of pilot credits and waive the standard early-termination penalty for the pilot SOW (non-standard).
3) Alignment to move to DocuSign with the redlined SOW and consumption forecast attached if approved.

Attachments: Medivio_consumption_forecast.xlsx, Pilot_scope_and_metrics.docx, Redlined_SOW_Medivio.pdf

Customer timeline: Procurement has asked to complete approvals by end of next week (2027-06-12) to start pilot 6/20.

Next step: need a quick yes/no or items to escalate to legal/finance. If you want, I can join a 15-min sync with Marcus and Mina today.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — 28% concession for Medivio pilot + regional rollout

Thanks for the write-up, Ben. A couple of quick clarifying points before I escalate to the exec queue:

- Is the 28% flat across token tiers or only for the pilot-specific tier? Please confirm final unit economics (attach a summary row).
- Confirm that SSO + SOC2 pieces are already validated — we can't move forward in EU without the data control commitments.
- The early-termination waiver is a sticky non-standard term. Can we limit that waiver to the pilot window only and auto-reinstate standard terms at full SOW?

Marcus — can you confirm P&L impact and whether Finance can live with 28% given the 18-month ramp and expected longer-term revenue? Mina, LMK if this is strategically prioritized for your book. Laura, please confirm CS readiness to support a multi-region pilot if this gets approved.

If everyone replies quickly I’ll prepare a short memo for exec review (one page: why, impact, mitigations).

Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Deal Desk Operations
Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — 28% concession for Medivio pilot + regional rollout

Irene / team —

Reviewed the forecast and the redlined SOW. A few finance notes:
- I need the one-line confirmed model showing pilot effective rate vs. standard rate and expected blended margin at projected volumes (Ben, can you populate the ‘‘expected blended unit margin'' cell in the attached forecast).
- If the 28% is applied only to pilot usage (and not to any production volumes post-SOW), Finance is more comfortable because it contains the concession to a bounded period.
- The early-termination waiver should be time-boxed to the pilot and include a cap on waived damages (we recommend a $50k cap).

I’ve attached the redlines I recommend (Redlined_SOW_Medivio.pdf) and a sample P&L summary in the spreadsheet. Once Ben updates the single-line blended view, I can produce the exec memo with quantified impact (loss in ARR run-rate vs. upside).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Exec approval request — 28% concession for Medivio pilot + regional rollout

Irene / Marcus —

Thanks — updated the consumption forecast with a blended-rate summary and added a note that the 28% concession applies to the pilot tier only (pilot usage line in the spreadsheet). See attached.

Customer confirmation: Emma from Medivio has agreed to the time-boxed waiver for the pilot only and accepts the $50k cap on waived early-termination damages. Procurement is aligned to an expedited signature if we get exec sign-off by end of day Monday (2027-06-07).

For executives: below is the proposed one-line ask for sign-off (copyable into an approval thread):

"Approve up to 28% off standard Hosted API usage rates for Medivio’s 60-day pilot (pilot tier only), provide 60 days of pilot credits, and accept a limited early-termination waiver capped at $50,000. Approval contingent on execution of the attached redlined SOW and the signed consumption forecast. This concession is limited to the pilot period; standard rates apply to production volumes after SOW execution."

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/abcdef1234567890
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5204234/DEAL-MEDI-20270605

Irene — if you’re happy with the memo I sent earlier, please escalate to the exec list for sign-off. I’m standing by to hop on a call.

—Ben
